author: m.kalinin
content: what i am missing in the write-up is a word about home stakers. PQ + Gasper will likely make home staking prohibitive, PQ + DC might relax the reqs but not sure

author: potuz
content:
> btw, could you share your spam protection solution for the smart contract?
The contract prevents spam by just having a gas fee, the 8282 contract on top of that increases the fee exponentially. I changed (or rather asked Claude, haven't even looked at the output of course, hoping that Felix or Bosul or Matt will add themselves as authors) it to also decrease with blocks without preregistrations, because the idea I think is to deploy the contract as soon as possible and not worry about forking the CL until ready.

author: m.kalinin
content: we have to include head votes regardless, for the sake of view merge. although, with additional delta and switching to TOB-SVD technique instead of view merge, votes might not be needed in block at all

author: potuz
content:
> what i am missing in the write-up is a word about home stakers. PQ + Gasper will likely make home staking prohibitive, PQ + DC might relax the reqs but not sure
I agree, but it's too soon though, when we get a POC we'll know if Gasper is viable, if it's not then we should move to DC, but DC, unless it's strictly needed, should be thought of an upgrade. If Gasper needs extra changes like seconds per slot, or slots per epoch, or whatever, we should just ditch it

author: m.kalinin
content: having no fork would be ideal, but then it would mean that an amount of data limited by the spam protection will stay in the EL storage until the CL fork. If this is few MBs per year then it's fine ofc

author: potuz
content: anyone can create a contract without fees and just add data to it cheaper anyway

author: m.kalinin
content: ofc, i think that even if it's 1GB we are fine in terms of the disk space consumed by EL. but if this is 1GB of junk then it will take some time for CL to process it as there is a payload size constraint. not sure how much do we care about it though; it demands analysis

author: potuz
content: Yeah, so what I thought that analisys look like is in terms of timelines. If we are targetting to consume 1K vals per block, we know we have about 1M vals to consume, and we will be aiming to fork by the end of 2027. Then we can safely target at x (think about x ~ 16) deposits per block. A spammer can never spam enough to forbid us from consuming the data, and we have an entire year to onboard the legitimate stake.

author: m.kalinin
content: Agree, except for the fork in 2027, it is very optimistic in my view. But that's a different thing. If we end up not delivering the entire fork in 2027, we can open up a reg on CL side at least
